item.title: Middle East war live: Trump claims he called off an Iran strike to allow for ‘serious negotiations’
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday claimed that he was holding off on a military strike on Iran planned for Tuesday at the request of Gulf State leaders because “serious negotiations” were under way. The president threatened that Washington was ready for a "full, large-scale assault of Iran” if an acceptable deal is not reached. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: South Korea and Japan’s Leaders Are Set to Meet: What to Know
item.description: Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, and South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, have surprised many observers by moving past their nations’ historical grievances.

item.title: Tuesday is a big primary day. Here's what you need to know
item.description: Six states are holding primaries May 19 that could help to decide the balance of power in Congress and in key state governments.

item.title: Israeli attacks in Gaza have stepped up since halt in bombing in Iran
item.description: At least five Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes on the Gaza Strip on May 17. Israel has stepped up attacks in Gaza in the weeks since halting its ​joint bombing ‌with the US in Iran. Netanyahu's government says Hamas fighters are tightening their grip on the strip. The devastated Palestinian territory has seen near-daily Israeli fire since the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas went into effect in October.

item.title: Trump Warns Iran the ‘Clock Is Ticking’ as Tensions Surge Again in Middle East
item.description: The president has sought to force Iran to accept his terms on its nuclear program or else face renewed war. An emboldened Iran has rebuffed Trump’s demands.

item.title: Most of the architects of October 7 attacks have been killed, says Netanyahu
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Sunday that Israel is close to finishing a key war aim in Gaza: killing the planners of the October 7 attacks. The comments came after Israel said it had killed senior Hamas commander Ezzedine Al-Haddad in an airstrike, as its campaign against the group’s leadership continues.

item.title: Millions Recovered in FIFA Corruption Scandal May Now Be Missing Again Before World Cup
item.description: Ahead of the World Cup, the head of South American soccer faces an ethics complaint he received payments recovered from a 2015 investigation that shook global soccer.

item.title: Trump Says He Authorized New Strikes on Iran, but Has Decided to Hold Off
item.description: President Trump has repeatedly threatened new military action against Iran, only to pull back from resuming major fighting in a deeply unpopular, expensive conflict.

item.title: The Supreme Court avoids taking up a fight over Voting Rights Act enforcement for now
item.description: After recently weakening the Voting Rights Act, the Supreme Court avoided for now taking up a legal question that may severely limit enforcement of the law's remaining protections for minority voters.
